content.title: About
content.content: Lima beans (Phaseolus lunatus) are large, buttery‑flavored legumes that are commonly sold canned in a light brine or mild sweetened liquid. They have a creamy texture and a subtle nutty taste when heated.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lima beans are also called “butter beans” because of their smooth texture.
They are among the largest edible beans, reaching up to 2 cm in length.
Originally cultivated in South America, especially Peru and Ecuador.
Canned beans are a convenient addition to salads, soups, and stews.
They provide a good source of carbohydrates and plant‑based protein.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Plant protein source
items.content: One cup of canned lima beans delivers about 10 g of protein, useful for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potassium aids fluid balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Lima beans provide thiamine, folate, and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: They cause a gradual rise in blood sugar, making them suitable for glycemic control.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans, including lima beans.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned varieties often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium options if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in very large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned lima beans can be tossed into salads, soups, chili, pasta dishes, or used as a filling for vegetable casseroles. Rinse them briefly under cold water before use to reduce excess salt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3–4 days. Discard if an off‑odor or mold appears.
